name: limit-bytes-at-limit
description: A definition of exactly the maximum 65,536 bytes parses and canonicalises normally: the definition-size cap does not fire at the boundary itself, only strictly above it.
notes: Padded to exactly 65,536 bytes with 1,024 distinct test/-prefixed refs (test/member-0000 through test/member-1023, each padded with filler to 60-61 code points) in a slot's set binding. The padding deliberately respects every other published limit so the byte boundary is the only thing at its edge: each ref is 60-61 code points, far under the 1,024-code-point string-length cap; 1,024 members is at, not over, the schema's set-members cap; nesting reaches depth 5 (root, slots array, slot object, binding object, refs array), not beyond; and there is one slot, well under the 64-slot cap. The refs are pairwise distinct so de-duplication cannot shrink the projection and mask the byte-boundary case under test. The padding length is computed mechanically from the fixed skeleton's byte length, never hand-counted.
